review_basis: Each original numbered Module 09 WebP in this part was individually viewed, with diagrams, example tables, numerical illustrations, AWS service references and decision cues traced in their visible order. Narration is grounded in those visuals.
part_title: SageMaker Studio and Visual Development Tools

scenes.title: SageMaker Studio
scenes.narration: SageMaker Studio is a browser-based environment for machine learning development. Follow the five large boxes across the middle of the slide. First, access Studio in a web browser. Second, develop in notebooks, which are interactive documents where a data scientist can write and run code while exploring data. Third, run training jobs using SageMaker resources. Fourth, manage the work by tracking experiments, comparing results and organizing model versions. Fifth, deploy the chosen model to an endpoint, where an application can request predictions. The bottom example runs this same sequence for customer churn: start with customer data, prepare and train, compare experiments, deploy, then predict which customers may leave. At the top right, compare Studio with SageMaker Canvas. Studio offers notebooks and a broader development environment for machine learning engineers, whereas Canvas emphasizes a visual no-code experience for business analysts. The decision is about the development workflow and user skills, not which tool guarantees a more accurate model.
